correctness.rationale: The verifier exhausts all complete strict profiles for n<=3 and all unilateral complete-list reports. At n=3 it checks 46,656 truthful profiles, uses two independent deferred-acceptance implementations, and separately enumerates all six true matchings whenever manipulation occurs. It reproduces 864 bad profiles, the 648/216 manipulator split, one profitable report per manipulating woman, true stability of every profitable outcome, and 24 symmetry classes by both canonicalization and Burnside counting.

evidence: Teo-Sethuraman-Tan derive an optimal single-woman complete-list cheating strategy and report random simulations, including 1000 random instances at size 8.
Shen-Deng-Tang study arbitrary coalitions and feasible stable outcomes via permutation manipulation.
Later work explicitly describes single-woman permutation manipulation as a separate algorithmic problem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General algorithms decide or construct manipulations, but they do not imply the exact fraction of all three-by-three truthful profiles, the manipulator multiplicities, or the symmetry-class count without a complete finite classification.

value.rationale: The result resolves the first market size at which complete-list receiver manipulation can occur and quantifies exactly how often it occurs. The one-versus-two manipulator split, unique profitable report, stability of every profitable outcome at the boundary, and exact symmetry quotient give a compact structural classification of a canonical deferred-acceptance incentive problem.
